canonical_name: Resilience Evaluation Scale (RES), final 9-item Simplified Chinese version
construct: self-perceived psychological resilience / internal coping resources

source.citation: Qing, Y., Bakker, A., van der Meer, C. A. I., te Brake, H., & Olff, M. (2022). Assessing psychological resilience: translation and validation of the Chinese version of the resilience evaluation scale (RES). European Journal of Psychotraumatology, 13(2), 2133358.

instructions.source_semantics: Rate agreement with statements about how you usually respond to difficult situations.
instructions.source_timeframe: Usual/general response; no past-week/month recall window specified.
instructions.implementation_zh_cn_working_text: 请根据自己通常如何应对困难情境，选择你对以下每项陈述的同意程度。
instructions.implementation_text_status: Project working translation/presentation, NOT a verbatim validated Chinese instruction. The 2022 article and its supplementary DOCX do not print the Chinese instruction or full Chinese response anchors.

response_option_provenance: 2022 section 2.2.2 establishes 0–4 and English endpoints. Five English labels in original van der Meer et al. 2018 scale/Appendix A. All Chinese option labels above are project working translations, not claimed verbatim from Qing et al. 2022.

scoring.formula: total = sum(RES1, RES2, RES3, RES4, RES5, RES6, RES7, RES8, RES9)
scoring.missing_data_rule: No validated missing-response rule located. Implementation policy: require all nine responses; do not score partial, impute, or prorate.
scoring.policy_vs_source: Requiring complete responses is conservative platform policy, not an imputation rule published by authors.

evidence.population: Adults in mainland China; predominantly female, young, highly educated Han-Chinese convenience sample
evidence.factor_evidence: Chinese parallel analysis retained one factor, 49.92% explained variance; the original two-factor CFA was adequate to mediocre.
limits: No Chinese test-retest study in this paper
No clinical cutoff or low/medium/high ranges established
Do not transfer original Dutch/English self-confidence/self-efficacy subscales to this Chinese implementation
No cross-language measurement-invariance or national norms established here

report.score_template: 你的 RES 自评总分为 {total}/36。分数越高，表示你通常对自己应对困难的能力评价越积极；它不是诊断，也不能证明你未来一定能或不能应对某种事件。
report.interpretation: 本量表没有经该研究验证的临床分界值，不划分高/中/低等级。一次自评分数会受到当时的处境和感受影响，也不涵盖所有外部支持与资源。
report.suggestion: 可以回顾一个最近遇到的困难，写下你已经采取的一项有效行动和可以寻求的一种支持。分数不理想不代表你软弱或失败。若困扰持续影响生活，可以与可信赖的人或专业人员讨论。
report.status: Original platform explanatory copy, not author-prescribed treatment or threshold interpretation.
